units.one_line: The `interfold` binary: parses commands, runs them locally, or forwards the allowed few to a node already running here.
units.explain: The binary is the operator's entry point: it parses the command, loads the config, then either forwards the command to a node already running on this machine or runs it in-process. Only rev (without --features), print-env, net get-peer-id, noir status, ciphernode status, events query and wallet get are forwarded; every other command runs in the calling process. `interfold start` takes the process fence, starts the control server, builds the node through the entrypoint crate, and starts the dashboard when a port is set. `interfold program compile`, `start` and `cache purge` live in `program_support.rs`: they run `cargo` for the `program-runner` binary of the project's `runner/` crate (`dev` or `openvm` mode), run the embedded `scripts/openvm-compile.sh` for an OpenVM compile, and refuse a project that still has `.interfold/support`.
units.analogy: A front desk that passes a request to the manager already on site when one is in, and otherwise handles it at the counter.

units.one_line: Operator-side library behind the node commands: starts a node from config, guards its data directory, and runs validation, purge and reset.
units.explain: `start::start::execute` is the production caller of the ciphernode builder: it loads the cipher from the key file, chooses the full or bootstrap settings, and waits for the build under the startup timeout. The rest of the crate holds what the CLI calls around a node: a process fence so one data directory has one live node, a `nodes` process manager that starts one `interfold start` child per configured profile, offline state validation, and purge and reset commands that refuse to delete key-share state for an unfinished E3. Without it the CLI could not start a node or change its state safely.
units.analogy: A site foreman: checks the site is free and the records are in order, hands the blueprint to the builder, and keeps the list of what is on site before anything is demolished.

units.one_line: Composition root that assembles one ciphernode: storage checks, event bus, chain listeners, sortition, protocol extensions, networking and startup sync.
units.explain: `CiphernodeBuilder` collects settings through `with_*` methods, and `build` runs startup in a fixed order: storage schema and role checks, reconciling restored E3 state with the chain, sortition, EVM listeners for each enabled chain, protocol extensions, networking, attaching the request router, then a wait for sync. Protocol extensions (threshold keyshare, aggregation, accusation and consistency checks) are registered on the router only for the roles that are switched on. A bootstrap role refuses keyshare, aggregation, and the full, registry and slashing contract components (it keeps only the Interfold reader), and gets no accusation or consistency extension.
units.analogy: An assembly line where each station is bolted on in a fixed order, and the line does not start until every station has passed its check.

units.one_line: Loopback control channel: a small HTTP server inside a running node that runs forwarded CLI commands, plus the client that sends them.
units.explain: While `interfold start` runs, `start_daemon_server` listens on 127.0.0.1 at the node's control port and answers each HTTP request with the output of one command. Another `interfold` process first probes that port with `connect_daemon`; if a node answers, it posts its command with `run_on_daemon` and prints the reply lines. Without it, a command could not reach the state of a node that is already running.
units.analogy: A switchboard extension inside a building: only callers in the same building (loopback) can reach it, and the office answers with the result.

units.one_line: Output sink for CLI commands: each line goes through a channel to a printer task, so output keeps its order and survives exit.
units.explain: Commands that use it call `log!` on a cloneable `Console`, which sends each line into an unbounded channel. A background task prints the lines in order to stdout or writes them to any async writer, and `channel()` lets the daemon collect a remote command's output instead. `flush` drops the sender and waits for the printer to drain, so nothing is lost when the process exits.
units.analogy: A post room: each letter goes into one tray in order, one clerk sends them all out, and the office closes only after the tray is empty.

units.one_line: Implements `interfold init`: fetches the project template at the release tag, pins package versions, copies it in, and installs packages.
units.explain: `execute` clones the template repository, by default at this CLI's own release tag, into a temporary folder, then copies it into the project through filters. The filters pin `@interfold/contracts`, `@interfold/react` and `@interfold/sdk` to the versions in that clone and rewrite Interfold crate path dependencies, such as `e3-program-runner`, to the template's git commit. It then runs `pnpm install` unless `--skip-install` is set, so a new project matches the release's contracts, SDK and program runner.
units.analogy: A flat-pack kit for this release: it fetches the parts for this version, adjusts the labels to fit, lays them out in the new room, and then runs the assembly step.

units.one_line: Small async file-system layer over the vfs crate, with a real-disk root and an in-memory root for tests.
units.explain: `Fs` wraps a `vfs` root and implements small async traits for reading, writing, creating directories, copying, finding files by glob, and replacing text in place. `Fs::physical()` roots these at the real file system and `Fs::mem()` at an in-memory tree, so the copier can run in tests without touching disk. Without it, the template copy in `interfold init` would call the disk directly and could not be tested in memory.
units.analogy: A stock room with two doors: the same clerk works in the real warehouse or in a scale model of it, depending on which door is used.

units.one_line: Installer for the interfold CLI: downloads the GitHub release binary that matches this OS and CPU, then installs, updates, or removes it.
units.explain: `interfoldup install` picks a release of theinterfold/interfold (the latest, the newest published one with `dev`, or a given tag), selects the asset whose name contains `interfold-<os>-<arch>`, and unpacks the gzip tarball. It writes the binary to `~/.local/bin`, or to `/usr/local/bin` with `--system`, and warns when that folder is not on PATH. `update` and `uninstall` use the same folders. Without it, an operator would have to find, unpack and place the release binary by hand.
units.analogy: A courier who fetches the build for your machine's OS and CPU from the warehouse, leaves it at your door, and collects the old one when asked.
